column1: # The mandatory block is positional and every parser agrees about it. The optional tags
# after it are `<key>-<value>`, and the key itself contains dashes: GP-Lat, GP-Lon,
# GP-Alt. Both ground parsers split on the last dash, which is the separator right up
# until the value is negative -- and then the last dash is the minus sign. `GP-Lat--18.5`
# split to the key `GP-Lat-` and the value `18.5`: the sign eaten, the key unrecognisable,
# so `gps_lat` read back as null and a southern-hemisphere fix vanished from the console,
# the CSV and the map with no error and no rejection counter.
# Both implementations were wrong in the same way, which is why no test caught it: they
# were hand-ports of one another and the fixtures had no negative coordinate. This file
# Format: <id> TAB <optional field as transmitted> TAB <expected key> TAB <expected value>
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.
# The cases that were broken. A southern latitude, a western longitude, an altitude below
# sea level, and a negative diagnostic value.
# A value that is only a minus sign is not a number, but it must not be mis-split either:
